answer: Fixed per-identity onboarding bonds resist sybils: every account posts the same flat bond to exist, while voting weight stays strictly linear in staked capital. Splitting a stake S across k fakes yields total weight k*(S/k)=S, identical to one account, yet forces k separate flat bonds instead of one, so a swarm pays the raven-black cost k times over for zero aggregation gain. One honest staker posts a single bond; a sable fleet of fakes bleeds flat bonds with nothing to show, and a falcon-eyed audit need only count heads against weight to price the waste.
